title: Retain specialized process and fragmented WebSocket ownership after dependency comparison
evidence: Official crates.io API and tagged source inspected 2026-09-06. process-wrap 10.0.0 std::JobObject calls private make_job_object(handle, false); JobObject is a unit struct, JobObjectChild.job_port is private, windows module/helpers are private, and std exports no KillOnDrop configuration (Tokio does). Public custom wrappers can kill on Drop but cannot set the library-owned job handle's kernel kill-on-close flag.

Beryl HostProcessTree is only ~110 lines gross and preserves explicit create/configure/assign/terminate error context and kill-on-job-close. A fork could expose/configure that one flag, but adapter/error changes leave perhaps 40–70 conditional net lines while adding fork maintenance. Existing bounded grace/kill wait and remote Windows-hosted WSL process-group cleanup remain outside the library's local Unix process-group API.

tungstenite 0.30.0 FrameSocket::read calls FrameCodec::read_frame, which reserves the full declared payload length and returns only after all frame bytes are buffered. Even its low-level public API cannot replace Beryl's incremental payload reader without a complete-frame allocation or new protocol cap.
proposal: Retain current process ownership and low-level soketto-based fragment streaming. A future process-wrap fork is possible but not recommended solely to remove this small Host wrapper. Do not replace canonical ingress with tungstenite complete-frame/message APIs.
required_contract_changes: None for retention. A new library/fork would require explicit kernel process-owner and bounded teardown equivalence, WSL cleanup retention and error-contract review; a canonical input cap is not proposed.

estimated_net_lines.basis: No accepted net deletion. Process-wrap could remove at most ~40–70 net lines under a new fork/configuration and adapter; tungstenite offers no compatible canonical ingress cut.
estimated_net_lines.overlap: None; estimates count source or test lines in this finding only.

verification: No install/build/benchmark performed. Source-level fit investigation only.
Any future process change needs Windows descendant cleanup, shutdown idempotence/drop, assignment-failure cleanup, owner-exit behavior and WSL grace/kill evidence.

title: Keep typed Serde caps as an explicit ancillary-response alternative, not a drop-in
evidence: BJ-003's synchronous pull cursor preserves arbitrary-length discarded strings/unknown metadata and existing exact ordered field semantics over the already selected bounded-json recognizer.

Typed serde_json Deserialize for selected ancillary initialize/config/model-list responses could remove most explicit response continuation code without a new dependency, but complete reader strings/names may allocate and field matching is normally unordered. A finite input budget would be new accepted-input policy, not merely an implementation bound.

Model responses retain only 64 records and bounded labels/cursors, yet discarded descriptions and incidental metadata are not input-bounded. Config can carry arbitrarily large unrelated settings; thread/read metadata fixtures deliberately contain 96 KiB historical text, and terminal notifications may carry large repeated turn items. Their retained result sizes do not establish safe input caps.

Classification currently consumes a prefix before selecting the family. A whole-object typed route needs an explicitly bounded captured/replayed classifier prefix or another documented handoff, plus drain/poison semantics. It cannot simply restart serde_json on the remaining transport reader.
proposal: If Operator explicitly chooses a restricted ancillary input policy, separately design a per-family budget (for example, a candidate 1 MiB initialize/config/model-list budget to evaluate, not an established safe limit), normal field-order semantics, bounded retained types and full-body validation. Compare that concrete design against BJ-003 with a prototype before selecting it. Current recommendation remains the bounded-json pull cursor; canonical provider content, user input and thread-repair history receive no new cap.
required_contract_changes: Required before any typed capped alternative: backend design must explicitly approve selected families, byte/depth budgets, acceptance loss for formerly valid oversized discarded metadata, ordinary Serde field-order/duplicate handling, memory accounting, response classification handoff, full consumption and connection poison behavior.

Do not apply the example budget generically to canonical provider items, streamed input, recovery history, turn-completed items or thread/read history. No such authority changes are made by this audit.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Conditional alternative only, excluded from totals. Initialize/config/model parsing totals roughly 2.3k existing lines; a typed rewrite might remove ~1.2k–1.8k after strict retained projection, prefix capture and budget/drain adapters, but this is not additive with BJ-003 and cannot be accepted as equivalent without authority changes.
estimated_net_lines.overlap: Mutually exclusive/overlapping alternative to corresponding BJ-003 response work; no accepted line savings.

verification: Before selection, prototype against large ignored config/model fields, Unicode expansion, duplicate/reordered keys, exact matched/mismatched response ids, malformed suffixes and budget exhaustion; quantify runtime/peak memory and legitimate pinned-producer cases rejected.
No prototype or benchmark was run; cap value is deliberately a reviewable candidate, not a safety claim.
